ko.title: [마케팅 101 #14] 나쁜 헤어컷은 반품할 수 없다: 서비스 마케팅과 글로벌 진출

segments.src: > When the product is a performance rather than a thing, quality becomes an experience you manage — and when you carry that experience across a border, you have to decide what stays the same and what bends.
segments.tr: > 제품이 물건이 아니라 성과(performance)일 때, 품질은 당신이 관리하는 경험이 된다 — 그리고 그 경험을 국경 너머로 가져갈 때, 무엇이 그대로 유지될지, 무엇이 변할지 결정해야 한다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Most of what Americans spend money on isn't a thing you can put in a box.
segments.tr: 미국인들이 돈을 쓰는 대부분의 것은 상자에 넣을 수 있는 물건이 아니다.

segments.src: Haircuts, flights, checking accounts, dental cleanings, software subscriptions, a table at a restaurant — services make up the large majority of U.S.
segments.tr: 헤어컷, 항공편, 당좌예금, 치과 청소, 소프트웨어 구독, 레스토랑의 테이블 — 서비스는 미국

segments.src: economic activity and employment.
segments.tr: 경제 활동과 고용의 대부분을 차지한다.

segments.src: Marketing them works differently, for four stubborn reasons:
segments.tr: 이들을 마케팅하는 것은 네 가지 근본적인 이유로 다르게 작동한다:

segments.src: - **Intangibility.** You can't inspect a service before you buy it. You can hold a pair of shoes; you can't hold a root canal.
segments.tr: - **무형성(Intangibility).** 서비스를 구매하기 전에 검사할 수 없다. 신발 한 켤레는 손에 들 수 있지만, 신경근관 치료는 들 수 없다.

segments.src: - **Heterogeneity (variability).** The same barista, same store, different Tuesday — different experience. Humans deliver services, so quality wobbles.
segments.tr: - **이질성(Heterogeneity, 다양성).** 같은 바리스타, 같은 가게, 다른 화요일 — 다른 경험. 인간이 서비스를 제공하므로 품질은 들쑥날쑥하다.

segments.src: - **Inseparability.** Production and consumption happen at the same time. The customer is *inside the factory*, and so are the other customers.
segments.tr: - **분리불가능성(Inseparability).** 생산과 소비가 동시에 발생한다. 고객이 *공장 내부에 있으며*, 다른 고객들도 마찬가지다.

segments.src: - **Perishability.** An empty seat on a 6:00 a.m. flight to Chicago can't be put in a warehouse and sold tomorrow. Unsold capacity is gone forever.
segments.tr: - **소멸성(Perishability).** 오전 6시 시카고행 비행기의 빈 좌석은 창고에 보관했다가 내일 팔 수 없다. 팔리지 않은 용량은 영구적으로 사라진다.

segments.src: Because of this, service firms don't manage "quality" the way a factory does.
segments.tr: 이 때문에 서비스 회사들은 공장처럼 '품질'을 관리하지 않는다.

segments.src: The dominant framework, **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman, Zeithaml, and Berry, 1988), says customers judge service on five dimensions — often remembered as **RATER**:
segments.tr: 지배적인 프레임워크인 **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman, Zeithaml, and Berry, 1988)은 고객이 서비스를 다섯 가지 차원으로 판단한다고 말하며 — 종종 **RATER**로 기억된다:

segments.src: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?
segments.tr: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?

segments.src: Assurance       - do staff seem competent and trustworthy?
segments.tr: Assurance       - do staff seem competent and trustworthy?

segments.src: Tangibles       - how do the space, equipment, and people look?
segments.tr: Tangibles       - how do the space, equipment, and people look?

segments.src: Empathy         - was I treated as an individual?
segments.tr: Empathy         - was I treated as an individual?

segments.src: Responsiveness  - were they willing to help, promptly?
segments.tr: Responsiveness  - were they willing to help, promptly?

segments.src: The core idea is a gap: `Service quality = perceived performance - expectation`.
segments.tr: 핵심 아이디어는 갭(gap)이다: `서비스 품질 = 지각된 성과 - 기대`.

segments.src: That's not a formula to compute so much as a warning.
segments.tr: 그것은 계산하는 공식이라기보다는 경고다.

segments.src: You can improve a service and still lose customers, if your advertising raised expectations faster than your operation improved.
segments.tr: 광고가 운영 개선보다 더 빠르게 기대를 높였다면, 서비스를 개선해도 고객을 잃을 수 있다.

segments.src: Under-promise is not a slogan; it's quality management.
segments.tr: 약속을 낮게 하는 것은 슬로건이 아니라 품질 관리다.

segments.src: Because a service is a performance, the classic **4P** marketing mix (product, price, place, promotion) leaves out too much.
segments.tr: 서비스가 성과이므로, 고전적인 **4P** 마케팅 믹스(product, price, place, promotion)는 너무 많은 것을 빠뜨린다.

segments.src: Booms and Bitner (1981) added three, giving the **extended 7Ps**:
segments.tr: Booms and Bitner (1981)는 세 가지를 추가하여 **확장된 7Ps**를 제시했다:

segments.src: - **People** — employees *are* the product. Front-line hiring and training is marketing spend, whether you book it that way or not.
segments.tr: - **사람(People)** — 직원들이 *바로* 제품이다. 최전선 채용과 교육은 당신이 그렇게 계상하든 하지 않든 마케팅 비용이다.

segments.src: - **Process** — the choreography of delivery: the online booking flow, the queue design, the way a refund is handled.
segments.tr: - **프로세스(Process)** — 제공의 안무: 온라인 예약 흐름, 대기열 설계, 환불이 처리되는 방식.

segments.src: - **Physical evidence** — the tangible cues that stand in for a product you can't see: the clean lobby, the branded cup, the confirmation email, the itemized receipt.
segments.tr: - **물리적 증거(Physical evidence)** — 볼 수 없는 제품을 대신하는 유형의 단서: 깨끗한 로비, 브랜드가 있는 컵, 확인 이메일, 항목별 영수증.

segments.src: **Global marketing** asks the same question one level up.
segments.tr: **글로벌 마케팅**은 한 단계 높은 수준에서 같은 질문을 던진다.

segments.src: When you take an offering abroad, you face two decisions.
segments.tr: 오퍼링을 해외로 가져갈 때, 당신은 두 가지 결정에 직면한다.

segments.src: **Decision 1: How much do you change?** Full **standardization** buys scale, a consistent brand, and lower cost.
segments.tr: **결정 1: 얼마나 변할 것인가?** 완전한 **표준화**는 규모, 일관된 브랜드, 낮은 비용을 얻는다.

segments.src: Full **adaptation** buys local fit.
segments.tr: 완전한 **적응**은 현지 적합성을 얻는다.

segments.src: Almost everyone lands in between — **"glocalization"** — standardizing the core (brand, quality standards, core process) while adapting the periphery (menu, pricing, media, service norms).
segments.tr: 거의 모두가 중간에 정착한다 — **"글로컬라이제이션"** — 핵심(브랜드, 품질 기준, 핵심 프로세스)은 표준화하면서 주변부(메뉴, 가격, 매체, 서비스 규범)는 적응시킨다.

segments.src: Tipping expectations, acceptable wait times, and how directly staff greet you all vary by country, and those are service attributes, not packaging.
segments.tr: 팁 기대, 수용 가능한 대기 시간, 직원이 얼마나 직접적으로 당신을 맞는 방식은 모두 나라마다 다르며, 이들은 서비스 속성이지 포장이 아니다.

segments.src: **Decision 2: How do you enter?** Entry modes trade control against risk and commitment, roughly in this order:
segments.tr: **결정 2: 어떻게 진입하는가?** 진입 모드는 통제와 위험 및 약속을 거래하며, 대략 이 순서대로다:

segments.src: Exporting            low control, low risk, low commitment
segments.tr: Exporting            low control, low risk, low commitment

segments.src: Licensing            partner uses your IP for a fee
segments.tr: Licensing            partner uses your IP for a fee

segments.src: Franchising          partner runs your format under your rules
segments.tr: Franchising          partner runs your format under your rules

segments.src: Joint venture        shared ownership with a local firm
segments.tr: Joint venture        shared ownership with a local firm

segments.src: Wholly owned sub.    full control, full risk (also called FDI)
segments.tr: Wholly owned sub.    full control, full risk (also called FDI)

segments.src: Services complicate this.
segments.tr: 서비스는 이를 복잡하게 한다.

segments.src: You can ship a container of sneakers; you can't ship a hotel stay.
segments.tr: 운동화 한 컨테이너는 배송할 수 있지만, 호텔 숙박은 배송할 수 없다.

segments.src: That's why service firms lean heavily on franchising, licensing, and joint ventures — they need people on the ground, and local partners bring real estate, regulatory knowledge, and labor practices you don't have.
segments.tr: 그 때문에 서비스 회사들은 가맹점, 라이선싱, 합작 투자에 크게 의존한다 — 그들은 현지에 있는 사람들이 필요하고, 현지 파트너는 당신이 가지지 않은 부동산, 규제 지식, 노동 관행을 가져온다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Think about a Starbucks run in your own neighborhood, then think about Starbucks in Italy.
segments.tr: 자신의 동네에서의 스타벅스 방문을 생각해보고, 이탈리아의 스타벅스를 생각해보자.

segments.src: Locally, the 7Ps are all visible.
segments.tr: 현지에서는 7Ps가 모두 눈에 띈다.

segments.src: The **product** is a $6 latte, but also a chair and Wi-Fi.
segments.tr: **제품**은 6달러 라떼이지만, 의자와 Wi-Fi도 포함된다.

segments.src: **People**: the barista who writes your name on the cup.
segments.tr: **사람**: 컵에 당신의 이름을 쓰는 바리스타.

segments.src: **Process**: mobile order-ahead, so the line isn't the experience.
segments.tr: **프로세스**: 모바일 미리 주문, 그래서 줄이 경험이 아니다.

segments.src: **Physical evidence**: the cup, the wood, the smell — tangible proof of an intangible thing.
segments.tr: **물리적 증거**: 컵, 나무, 냄새 — 무형의 것에 대한 유형의 증거.

segments.src: And **perishability** is why afternoon promotions exist at all; a 2:00 p.m.
segments.tr: 그리고 **소멸성**이 오후 프로모션이 존재하는 이유다; 오후 2시

segments.src: empty store is unrecoverable revenue, so you discount to shift demand into the trough rather than build more capacity for the 8:00 a.m.
segments.tr: 비어있는 가게는 회복할 수 없는 수익이므로, 오전 8시 피크에 대한 더 많은 용량을 구축하기보다는 할인으로 수요를 저점으로 이동시킨다.

segments.src: peak.
segments.tr: 피크.

segments.src: Now go global.
segments.tr: 이제 글로벌로 가보자.

segments.src: Starbucks entered Italy — a country with its own centuries-old espresso bar culture — only in September 2018, opening a Reserve Roastery in Milan rather than a standard store.
segments.tr: 스타벅스는 자체적인 수백 년 된 에스프레소 바 문화를 가진 나라인 이탈리아에 2018년 9월에만 진입했으며, 표준 매장보다는 밀라노에 리저브 로스터리를 개설했다.

segments.src: That's glocalization: keep the brand and quality standards, change the format and the pitch.
segments.tr: 그것이 글로컬라이제이션이다: 브랜드와 품질 기준을 유지하고, 형식과 피치는 바꾼다.

segments.src: Elsewhere, Starbucks has used a mix of entry modes rather than one: company-owned stores in some markets, licensed stores operated by local partners in others, and a 50/50 joint venture with the Tata group in India (formed in 2012), where a local partner brought real estate and sourcing that a foreign entrant couldn't assemble quickly.
segments.tr: 다른 곳에서는 스타벅스가 하나의 진입 모드보다는 혼합을 사용했다: 어떤 시장에서는 회사 소유 매장, 다른 시장에서는 현지 파트너가 운영하는 라이선스 매장, 그리고 인도의 타타 그룹과의 50/50 합작 투자(2012년 설립)로, 현지 파트너가 외국 진입자가 빠르게 조립할 수 없었던 부동산과 소싱을 가져왔다.

segments.src: The lesson isn't "copy Starbucks."
segments.tr: 그 교훈은 "스타벅스를 따라 하라"는 것이 아니다.

segments.src: It's that the same two questions — *what do we standardize?* and *how much control do we need on the ground?* — are the whole game, whether you're a coffee chain, a dental practice opening a second location in another state, or a SaaS company hiring its first support team in Berlin.
segments.tr: 같은 두 질문 — *우리가 무엇을 표준화할 것인가?*와 *현지에서 우리가 얼마나 많은 통제가 필요한가?* — 이 전부다, 당신이 커피 체인이든, 다른 주에 두 번째 위치를 개설하는 치과 진료소든, 또는 베를린에서 첫 번째 지원 팀을 고용하는 SaaS 회사든 상관없이.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Services are intangible, variable, inseparable from delivery, and perishable — so quality is judged as *perceived performance minus expectation*, across five dimensions (RATER).
segments.tr: 1. 서비스는 무형이며, 가변적이고, 전달과 분리불가능하며, 소멸하는 것이다 — 따라서 품질은 *지각된 성과 빼기 기대*로 판단되며, 다섯 가지 차원(RATER)에 걸쳐 있다.

segments.src: 2. The 4Ps stretch to 7Ps for services: add people, process, and physical evidence — because employees and choreography *are* the product.
segments.tr: 2. 4Ps는 서비스를 위해 7Ps로 확장된다: 사람, 프로세스, 물리적 증거를 추가하라 — 직원과 안무가 *바로* 제품이기 때문이다.

segments.src: 3. Going global means choosing how much to standardize versus adapt, and choosing an entry mode along the control-versus-risk ladder; service firms lean toward franchising, licensing, and joint ventures because delivery can't be exported.
segments.tr: 3. 글로벌로 가는 것은 표준화와 적응의 수준을 선택하고, 통제 대 위험 사다리에 따라 진입 모드를 선택하는 것을 의미한다; 서비스 회사들은 전달을 수출할 수 없기 때문에 가맹점, 라이선싱, 합작 투자로 치우친다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 진단

segments.src: **1.** An airline can't store today's unsold seats to sell next week.
segments.tr: **1.** 항공사는 오늘의 팔리지 않은 좌석을 다음 주에 팔기 위해 보관할 수 없다.

segments.src: Which characteristic of services is this?
segments.tr: 서비스의 어떤 특성인가?

segments.src: - (a) Intangibility
segments.tr: - (a) 무형성

segments.src: - (b) Heterogeneity
segments.tr: - (b) 이질성

segments.src: - (c) Perishability
segments.tr: - (c) 소멸성

segments.src: - (d) Inseparability
segments.tr: - (d) 분리불가능성

segments.src: **2.** Which three Ps are added to the classic 4Ps to form the extended services marketing mix?
segments.tr: **2.** 확장된 서비스 마케팅 믹스를 형성하기 위해 고전적인 4Ps에 어떤 세 가지 P가 추가되는가?

segments.src: - (a) People, Process, Physical evidence
segments.tr: - (a) 사람, 프로세스, 물리적 증거

segments.src: - (b) Positioning, Packaging, Personalization
segments.tr: - (b) 포지셔닝, 패키징, 개인화

segments.src: - (c) People, Profit, Placement
segments.tr: - (c) 사람, 수익, 배치

segments.src: - (d) Process, Partnership, Performance
segments.tr: - (d) 프로세스, 파트너십, 성과

segments.src: **3.** O/X: A joint venture gives a company more control over foreign operations than exporting does, but also carries more risk and commitment.
segments.tr: **3.** O/X: 합작 투자는 수출보다 외국 사업에 대해 회사에 더 많은 통제를 제공하지만, 더 많은 위험과 약속도 수반한다.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **SERVQUAL** — A framework measuring service quality as the gap between customer expectations and perceptions, across five dimensions (reliability, assurance, tangibles, empathy, responsiveness).
segments.tr: - **SERVQUAL** — 고객 기대와 지각 사이의 갭으로서 서비스 품질을 측정하는 프레임워크로, 다섯 가지 차원(신뢰성, 보증, 유형성, 공감, 반응성)에 걸쳐 있다.

segments.src: - **Perishability** — The property that unused service capacity cannot be inventoried; unsold capacity is lost permanently.
segments.tr: - **소멸성** — 사용하지 않은 서비스 용량을 재고로 유지할 수 없는 특성; 팔리지 않은 용량은 영구적으로 손실된다.

segments.src: - **Extended 7Ps** — The services marketing mix: the 4Ps plus people, process, and physical evidence.
segments.tr: - **확장된 7Ps** — 서비스 마케팅 믹스: 4Ps에 사람, 프로세스, 물리적 증거를 더한 것.

segments.src: - **Physical evidence** — Tangible cues (facilities, uniforms, receipts, packaging) that customers use to infer the quality of an intangible service.
segments.tr: - **물리적 증거** — 고객이 무형 서비스의 품질을 추론하는 데 사용하는 유형의 단서(시설, 유니폼, 영수증, 패키징).

segments.src: - **Glocalization** — Standardizing a global brand's core while adapting local elements such as menu, pricing, and communication.
segments.tr: - **글로컬라이제이션** — 메뉴, 가격, 커뮤니케이션과 같은 현지 요소를 적응시키면서 글로벌 브랜드의 핵심을 표준화하는 것.

segments.src: - **Entry mode** — The structural choice for entering a foreign market (exporting, licensing, franchising, joint venture, wholly owned subsidiary), trading control against risk and commitment.
segments.tr: - **진입 모드** — 외국 시장에 진입하기 위한 구조적 선택(수출, 라이선싱, 가맹점, 합작 투자, 완전 소유 자회사)으로, 통제와 위험 및 약속을 거래한다.

zh.title: [营销101 #14] 你不能退回坏理发：服务营销和全球拓展

segments.src: > When the product is a performance rather than a thing, quality becomes an experience you manage — and when you carry that experience across a border, you have to decide what stays the same and what bends.
segments.tr: > 当产品是一种表现而非实物时，质量变成了你需要管理的体验——当你跨越边界带去这种体验时，你必须决定什么保持不变，什么需要灵活调整。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Most of what Americans spend money on isn't a thing you can put in a box.
segments.tr: 美国人花钱的大部分不是你能装进盒子的实物。

segments.src: Haircuts, flights, checking accounts, dental cleanings, software subscriptions, a table at a restaurant — services make up the large majority of U.S.
segments.tr: 理发、航班、支票账户、牙齿清洁、软件订阅、餐厅的一张桌子——服务构成了美国经济活动和就业的绝大多数。

segments.src: economic activity and employment.
segments.tr: 经济活动和就业。

segments.src: Marketing them works differently, for four stubborn reasons:
segments.tr: 营销它们的方式不同，原因有四个：

segments.src: - **Intangibility.** You can't inspect a service before you buy it. You can hold a pair of shoes; you can't hold a root canal.
segments.tr: - **无形性。** 你在购买前无法检查服务。你可以拿着一双鞋；你不能拿着根管治疗。

segments.src: - **Heterogeneity (variability).** The same barista, same store, different Tuesday — different experience. Humans deliver services, so quality wobbles.
segments.tr: - **异质性（可变性）。** 同样的咖啡师、同样的店铺、不同的星期二——不同的体验。人类提供服务，所以质量会波动。

segments.src: - **Inseparability.** Production and consumption happen at the same time. The customer is *inside the factory*, and so are the other customers.
segments.tr: - **不可分离性。** 生产和消费同时发生。客户*在工厂内部*，其他客户也是。

segments.src: - **Perishability.** An empty seat on a 6:00 a.m. flight to Chicago can't be put in a warehouse and sold tomorrow. Unsold capacity is gone forever.
segments.tr: - **易消耗性。** 早上6点飞往芝加哥航班上的空座位无法放进仓库并在明天出售。未售出的容量永远消失了。

segments.src: Because of this, service firms don't manage "quality" the way a factory does.
segments.tr: 正因如此，服务公司不像工厂那样管理"质量"。

segments.src: The dominant framework, **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman, Zeithaml, and Berry, 1988), says customers judge service on five dimensions — often remembered as **RATER**:
segments.tr: 主流框架**SERVQUAL**（Parasuraman、Zeithaml和Berry，1988）说客户在五个维度上判断服务——通常记为**RATER**：

segments.src: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?
segments.tr: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?

segments.src: Assurance       - do staff seem competent and trustworthy?
segments.tr: Assurance       - do staff seem competent and trustworthy?

segments.src: Tangibles       - how do the space, equipment, and people look?
segments.tr: Tangibles       - how do the space, equipment, and people look?

segments.src: Empathy         - was I treated as an individual?
segments.tr: Empathy         - was I treated as an individual?

segments.src: Responsiveness  - were they willing to help, promptly?
segments.tr: Responsiveness  - were they willing to help, promptly?

segments.src: The core idea is a gap: `Service quality = perceived performance - expectation`.
segments.tr: 核心理念是一个差距：`服务质量 = 感知表现 - 期望`。

segments.src: That's not a formula to compute so much as a warning.
segments.tr: 这与其说是一个要计算的公式，不如说是一个警告。

segments.src: You can improve a service and still lose customers, if your advertising raised expectations faster than your operation improved.
segments.tr: 你可以改进一项服务但仍然失去客户，如果你的广告提高期望的速度比你的运营改进的速度更快。

segments.src: Under-promise is not a slogan; it's quality management.
segments.tr: 承诺不足不是一句标语；它是质量管理。

segments.src: Because a service is a performance, the classic **4P** marketing mix (product, price, place, promotion) leaves out too much.
segments.tr: 因为服务是一种表现，经典的**4P**营销组合（产品、价格、地点、促销）遗漏了太多。

segments.src: Booms and Bitner (1981) added three, giving the **extended 7Ps**:
segments.tr: Booms和Bitner（1981）添加了三个，形成了**扩展的7Ps**：

segments.src: - **People** — employees *are* the product. Front-line hiring and training is marketing spend, whether you book it that way or not.
segments.tr: - **人员** ——员工*就是*产品。前线招聘和培训是营销支出，无论你是否这样计账。

segments.src: - **Process** — the choreography of delivery: the online booking flow, the queue design, the way a refund is handled.
segments.tr: - **流程** ——交付的编排：在线预订流程、队列设计、退款处理方式。

segments.src: - **Physical evidence** — the tangible cues that stand in for a product you can't see: the clean lobby, the branded cup, the confirmation email, the itemized receipt.
segments.tr: - **物理证据** ——代表你看不到的产品的有形线索：干净的大厅、带品牌的杯子、确认邮件、逐项收据。

segments.src: **Global marketing** asks the same question one level up.
segments.tr: **全球营销**在更高层次上提出同样的问题。

segments.src: When you take an offering abroad, you face two decisions.
segments.tr: 当你把产品拓展到国外时，你面临两个决定。

segments.src: **Decision 1: How much do you change?** Full **standardization** buys scale, a consistent brand, and lower cost.
segments.tr: **决定1：你改变多少？** 完全**标准化**可以实现规模化、品牌一致和降低成本。

segments.src: Full **adaptation** buys local fit.
segments.tr: 完全**本地适应**可以实现本地契合。

segments.src: Almost everyone lands in between — **"glocalization"** — standardizing the core (brand, quality standards, core process) while adapting the periphery (menu, pricing, media, service norms).
segments.tr: 几乎每家公司都选择介于两者之间——**"全球本地化"**——标准化核心（品牌、质量标准、核心流程）同时适应外围（菜单、定价、媒体、服务规范）。

segments.src: Tipping expectations, acceptable wait times, and how directly staff greet you all vary by country, and those are service attributes, not packaging.
segments.tr: 小费期望、可接受的等待时间和员工如何问候你在不同国家都不同，这些是服务属性，而不是包装。

segments.src: **Decision 2: How do you enter?** Entry modes trade control against risk and commitment, roughly in this order:
segments.tr: **决定2：你如何进入？** 进入模式在控制和风险承诺之间权衡，大致顺序如下：

segments.src: Exporting            low control, low risk, low commitment
segments.tr: Exporting            low control, low risk, low commitment

segments.src: Licensing            partner uses your IP for a fee
segments.tr: Licensing            partner uses your IP for a fee

segments.src: Franchising          partner runs your format under your rules
segments.tr: Franchising          partner runs your format under your rules

segments.src: Joint venture        shared ownership with a local firm
segments.tr: Joint venture        shared ownership with a local firm

segments.src: Wholly owned sub.    full control, full risk (also called FDI)
segments.tr: Wholly owned sub.    full control, full risk (also called FDI)

segments.src: Services complicate this.
segments.tr: 服务使这变得复杂。

segments.src: You can ship a container of sneakers; you can't ship a hotel stay.
segments.tr: 你可以运送一个集装箱的运动鞋；你不能运送一次酒店住宿。

segments.src: That's why service firms lean heavily on franchising, licensing, and joint ventures — they need people on the ground, and local partners bring real estate, regulatory knowledge, and labor practices you don't have.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么服务公司大量依靠特许经营、许可和合资企业——他们需要现地人员，当地合作伙伴带来了你没有的房地产、监管知识和劳动力实践。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: Think about a Starbucks run in your own neighborhood, then think about Starbucks in Italy.
segments.tr: 想想你所在社区的星巴克，再想想意大利的星巴克。

segments.src: Locally, the 7Ps are all visible.
segments.tr: 在本地，这7Ps都是可见的。

segments.src: The **product** is a $6 latte, but also a chair and Wi-Fi.
segments.tr: **产品**是一杯$6的拿铁，但也包括椅子和Wi-Fi。

segments.src: **People**: the barista who writes your name on the cup.
segments.tr: **人员**：在杯子上写下你的名字的咖啡师。

segments.src: **Process**: mobile order-ahead, so the line isn't the experience.
segments.tr: **流程**：移动提前订购，所以排队不是体验。

segments.src: **Physical evidence**: the cup, the wood, the smell — tangible proof of an intangible thing.
segments.tr: **物理证据**：杯子、木头、气味——无形事物的有形证明。

segments.src: And **perishability** is why afternoon promotions exist at all; a 2:00 p.m.
segments.tr: 而**易消耗性**正是为什么下午促销存在；下午2点的

segments.src: empty store is unrecoverable revenue, so you discount to shift demand into the trough rather than build more capacity for the 8:00 a.m.
segments.tr: 空荡荡的店铺是无法收回的收入，所以你用打折来将需求转向低谷，而不是为早上8点的

segments.src: peak.
segments.tr: 高峰建设更多容量。

segments.src: Now go global.
segments.tr: 现在走向全球。

segments.src: Starbucks entered Italy — a country with its own centuries-old espresso bar culture — only in September 2018, opening a Reserve Roastery in Milan rather than a standard store.
segments.tr: 星巴克仅在2018年9月进入意大利——一个拥有自己数百年历史的浓缩咖啡吧文化的国家——在米兰开设了一家精品烘焙店而非标准店。

segments.src: That's glocalization: keep the brand and quality standards, change the format and the pitch.
segments.tr: 那就是全球本地化：保持品牌和质量标准，改变格式和推销方式。

segments.src: Elsewhere, Starbucks has used a mix of entry modes rather than one: company-owned stores in some markets, licensed stores operated by local partners in others, and a 50/50 joint venture with the Tata group in India (formed in 2012), where a local partner brought real estate and sourcing that a foreign entrant couldn't assemble quickly.
segments.tr: 在其他地方，星巴克使用了多种进入模式而不是单一模式：在某些市场拥有自己的店铺，在其他市场有当地合作伙伴经营的许可店铺，以及与印度塔塔集团的50/50合资企业（成立于2012年），当地合作伙伴提供了外来进入者无法迅速获得的房地产和采购。

segments.src: The lesson isn't "copy Starbucks."
segments.tr: 教训不是"复制星巴克"。

segments.src: It's that the same two questions — *what do we standardize?* and *how much control do we need on the ground?* — are the whole game, whether you're a coffee chain, a dental practice opening a second location in another state, or a SaaS company hiring its first support team in Berlin.
segments.tr: 关键是同样的两个问题——*我们标准化什么？* 和 *我们需要多少现地控制？* ——是整个游戏，无论你是咖啡连锁店、在另一个州开设第二家分店的牙科诊所，还是在柏林招聘第一支客服团队的SaaS公司。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Services are intangible, variable, inseparable from delivery, and perishable — so quality is judged as *perceived performance minus expectation*, across five dimensions (RATER).
segments.tr: 1. 服务是无形的、可变的、不可与交付分离的，且易消耗的——因此质量被判断为*感知表现减去期望*，跨越五个维度（RATER）。

segments.src: 2. The 4Ps stretch to 7Ps for services: add people, process, and physical evidence — because employees and choreography *are* the product.
segments.tr: 2. 服务的4Ps扩展到7Ps：添加人员、流程和物理证据——因为员工和编排*就是*产品。

segments.src: 3. Going global means choosing how much to standardize versus adapt, and choosing an entry mode along the control-versus-risk ladder; service firms lean toward franchising, licensing, and joint ventures because delivery can't be exported.
segments.tr: 3. 全球拓展意味着选择多少标准化与适应，以及沿控制-风险阶梯选择进入模式；服务公司倾向特许经营、许可和合资企业，因为交付无法出口。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测

segments.src: **1.** An airline can't store today's unsold seats to sell next week.
segments.tr: **1.** 航空公司无法将今天未售出的座位存放在仓库并在下周出售。

segments.src: Which characteristic of services is this?
segments.tr: 这是服务的哪个特征？

segments.src: - (a) Intangibility
segments.tr: - (a) 无形性

segments.src: - (b) Heterogeneity
segments.tr: - (b) 异质性

segments.src: - (c) Perishability
segments.tr: - (c) 易消耗性

segments.src: - (d) Inseparability
segments.tr: - (d) 不可分离性

segments.src: **2.** Which three Ps are added to the classic 4Ps to form the extended services marketing mix?
segments.tr: **2.** 哪三个P被添加到经典4Ps以形成扩展的服务营销组合？

segments.src: - (a) People, Process, Physical evidence
segments.tr: - (a) 人员、流程、物理证据

segments.src: - (b) Positioning, Packaging, Personalization
segments.tr: - (b) 定位、包装、个性化

segments.src: - (c) People, Profit, Placement
segments.tr: - (c) 人员、利润、位置

segments.src: - (d) Process, Partnership, Performance
segments.tr: - (d) 流程、伙伴关系、绩效

segments.src: **3.** O/X: A joint venture gives a company more control over foreign operations than exporting does, but also carries more risk and commitment.
segments.tr: **3.** 是/否：合资企业比出口给公司对海外运营提供更多控制，但也承担更多风险和承诺。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **SERVQUAL** — A framework measuring service quality as the gap between customer expectations and perceptions, across five dimensions (reliability, assurance, tangibles, empathy, responsiveness).
segments.tr: - **SERVQUAL** ——衡量服务质量的框架，将其定义为客户期望与感知之间的差距，跨越五个维度（可靠性、保证、有形性、同理心、响应性）。

segments.src: - **Perishability** — The property that unused service capacity cannot be inventoried; unsold capacity is lost permanently.
segments.tr: - **易消耗性** ——未使用的服务容量无法库存的特性；未售出的容量永久丧失。

segments.src: - **Extended 7Ps** — The services marketing mix: the 4Ps plus people, process, and physical evidence.
segments.tr: - **扩展的7Ps** ——服务营销组合：4Ps加人员、流程和物理证据。

segments.src: - **Physical evidence** — Tangible cues (facilities, uniforms, receipts, packaging) that customers use to infer the quality of an intangible service.
segments.tr: - **物理证据** ——有形线索（设施、制服、收据、包装），客户用来推断无形服务质量的信息。

segments.src: - **Glocalization** — Standardizing a global brand's core while adapting local elements such as menu, pricing, and communication.
segments.tr: - **全球本地化** ——标准化全球品牌的核心同时适应本地元素如菜单、定价和沟通。

segments.src: - **Entry mode** — The structural choice for entering a foreign market (exporting, licensing, franchising, joint venture, wholly owned subsidiary), trading control against risk and commitment.
segments.tr: - **进入模式** ——进入外国市场的结构选择（出口、许可、特许经营、合资企业、全资子公司），在控制与风险承诺之间权衡。

segments.src: *Answers: 1 — (c) Perishability.
segments.tr: *答案：1——(c) 易消耗性。

segments.src: Services are consumed as they're produced, so idle capacity can't be stored; this is why airlines, hotels, and salons manage demand with time-based pricing.
segments.tr: 服务在生产时被消费，所以闲置容量无法存储；这就是为什么航空公司、酒店和沙龙用基于时间的定价来管理需求。

segments.src: 2 — (a) People, Process, Physical evidence, added by Booms and Bitner (1981) precisely because service delivery depends on staff, choreography, and tangible cues.
segments.tr: 2——(a) 人员、流程、物理证据，由Booms和Bitner（1981）添加，正是因为服务交付取决于员工、编排和有形线索。

segments.src: Entry modes form a ladder: exporting is low control and low risk; a joint venture shares ownership and gives more operational control, but commits capital and exposes you to partner and market risk; a wholly owned subsidiary sits at the far end of both.*
segments.tr: 进入模式形成一个阶梯：出口是低控制和低风险；合资企业共享所有权并提供更多操作控制，但需要承诺资本并使你面临合作伙伴和市场风险；全资子公司处于两者光谱的最远端。*

segments.src: > When the product is a performance rather than a thing, quality becomes an experience you manage — and when you carry that experience across a border, you have to decide what stays the same and what bends.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Most of what Americans spend money on isn't a thing you can put in a box.
segments.tr: अमेरिकियों जो कुछ पैसे खर्च करते हैं उसमें से अधिकांश एक चीज़ नहीं है जिसे आप एक डिब्बे में डाल सकते हैं।

segments.src: Haircuts, flights, checking accounts, dental cleanings, software subscriptions, a table at a restaurant — services make up the large majority of U.S.
segments.tr: बाल कटवाना, उड़ानें, चेकिंग खाते, दंत सफाई, सॉफ़्टवेयर सदस्यता, रेस्तरां में एक टेबल — सेवाएं अमेरिकी

segments.src: economic activity and employment.
segments.tr: आर्थिक गतिविधि और रोजगार का एक बड़ा हिस्सा बनाती हैं।

segments.src: Marketing them works differently, for four stubborn reasons:
segments.tr: उन्हें बाजार में लाना अलग तरीके से काम करता है, चार दृढ़ कारणों से:

segments.src: - **Intangibility.** You can't inspect a service before you buy it. You can hold a pair of shoes; you can't hold a root canal.
segments.tr: - **अमूर्तता।** आप खरीदने से पहले किसी सेवा का निरीक्षण नहीं कर सकते। आप जूतों की एक जोड़ी पकड़ सकते हैं; आप रूट कैनाल नहीं पकड़ सकते।

segments.src: - **Heterogeneity (variability).** The same barista, same store, different Tuesday — different experience. Humans deliver services, so quality wobbles.
segments.tr: - **विविधता (परिवर्तनशीलता)।** वही बारिस्ता, वही स्टोर, अलग मंगलवार — अलग अनुभव। मनुष्य सेवाएं प्रदान करते हैं, इसलिए गुणवत्ता में उतार-चढ़ाव होता है।

segments.src: - **Inseparability.** Production and consumption happen at the same time. The customer is *inside the factory*, and so are the other customers.
segments.tr: - **अविभाज्यता।** उत्पादन और खपत एक ही समय में होती है। ग्राहक *कारखाने के अंदर* है, और अन्य ग्राहक भी हैं।

segments.src: - **Perishability.** An empty seat on a 6:00 a.m. flight to Chicago can't be put in a warehouse and sold tomorrow. Unsold capacity is gone forever.
segments.tr: - **नाशवानता।** शिकागो की 6:00 a.m. उड़ान पर एक खाली सीट को एक गोदाम में नहीं रखा जा सकता और कल बेचा जा सकता है। बिना बिकी क्षमता हमेशा के लिए चली जाती है।

segments.src: Because of this, service firms don't manage "quality" the way a factory does.
segments.tr: इसके कारण, सेवा कंपनियां "गुणवत्ता" को उस तरह प्रबंधित नहीं करती हैं जैसे एक कारखाना करता है।

segments.src: The dominant framework, **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman, Zeithaml, and Berry, 1988), says customers judge service on five dimensions — often remembered as **RATER**:
segments.tr: प्रमुख ढांचा, **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman, Zeithaml, and Berry, 1988), कहता है कि ग्राहक सेवा को पांच आयामों पर न्याय करते हैं — अक्सर **RATER** के रूप में याद किया जाता है:

segments.src: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?
segments.tr: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?

segments.src: Assurance       - do staff seem competent and trustworthy?
segments.tr: Assurance       - do staff seem competent and trustworthy?

segments.src: Tangibles       - how do the space, equipment, and people look?
segments.tr: Tangibles       - how do the space, equipment, and people look?

segments.src: Empathy         - was I treated as an individual?
segments.tr: Empathy         - was I treated as an individual?

segments.src: Responsiveness  - were they willing to help, promptly?
segments.tr: Responsiveness  - were they willing to help, promptly?

segments.src: The core idea is a gap: `Service quality = perceived performance - expectation`.
segments.tr: मूल विचार एक अंतराल है: `सेवा गुणवत्ता = माना गया प्रदर्शन - अपेक्षा`।

segments.src: That's not a formula to compute so much as a warning.
segments.tr: यह गणना करने के लिए उतना सूत्र नहीं है जितना एक चेतावनी है।

segments.src: You can improve a service and still lose customers, if your advertising raised expectations faster than your operation improved.
segments.tr: आप एक सेवा में सुधार कर सकते हैं और फिर भी ग्राहकों को खो सकते हैं, यदि आपके विज्ञापन ने आपके संचालन में सुधार होने से अधिक तेजी से अपेक्षाएं बढ़ाईं।

segments.src: Under-promise is not a slogan; it's quality management.
segments.tr: कम वादा करना एक नारा नहीं है; यह गुणवत्ता प्रबंधन है।

segments.src: Because a service is a performance, the classic **4P** marketing mix (product, price, place, promotion) leaves out too much.
segments.tr: क्योंकि एक सेवा एक प्रदर्शन है, क्लासिक **4P** मार्केटिंग मिश्रण (उत्पाद, मूल्य, स्थान, प्रचार) बहुत कुछ छोड़ देता है।

segments.src: Booms and Bitner (1981) added three, giving the **extended 7Ps**:
segments.tr: Booms और Bitner (1981) ने तीन जोड़े, **विस्तारित 7Ps**:

segments.src: - **People** — employees *are* the product. Front-line hiring and training is marketing spend, whether you book it that way or not.
segments.tr: - **लोग** — कर्मचारी *उत्पाद हैं*। अग्रभाग की नियुक्ति और प्रशिक्षण मार्केटिंग व्यय है, चाहे आप इसे इस तरह बुक करें या न करें।

segments.src: - **Process** — the choreography of delivery: the online booking flow, the queue design, the way a refund is handled.
segments.tr: - **प्रक्रिया** — वितरण की कोरियोग्राफी: ऑनलाइन बुकिंग प्रवाह, कतार डिज़ाइन, रिफंड को संभालने का तरीका।

segments.src: - **Physical evidence** — the tangible cues that stand in for a product you can't see: the clean lobby, the branded cup, the confirmation email, the itemized receipt.
segments.tr: - **भौतिक साक्ष्य** — मूर्त संकेत जो एक ऐसे उत्पाद के लिए खड़े होते हैं जिसे आप नहीं देख सकते: स्वच्छ लॉबी, ब्रांडेड कप, पुष्टिकरण ईमेल, विस्तृत रसीद।

segments.src: **Global marketing** asks the same question one level up.
segments.tr: **वैश्विक विपणन** एक स्तर ऊपर एक ही सवाल पूछता है।

segments.src: When you take an offering abroad, you face two decisions.
segments.tr: जब आप विदेश में एक प्रस्ताव ले जाते हैं, तो आपको दो निर्णयों का सामना करना पड़ता है।

segments.src: **Decision 1: How much do you change?** Full **standardization** buys scale, a consistent brand, and lower cost.
segments.tr: **निर्णय 1: आप कितना बदलते हैं?** पूर्ण **मानकीकरण** पैमाने, एक सुसंगत ब्रांड, और कम लागत खरीदता है।

segments.src: Full **adaptation** buys local fit.
segments.tr: पूर्ण **अनुकूलन** स्थानीय फिट खरीदता है।

segments.src: Almost everyone lands in between — **"glocalization"** — standardizing the core (brand, quality standards, core process) while adapting the periphery (menu, pricing, media, service norms).
segments.tr: लगभग हर कोई बीच में उतरता है — **"ग्लोकलाइजेशन"** — केंद्र (ब्रांड, गुणवत्ता मानदंड, मुख्य प्रक्रिया) को मानकीकृत करते हुए परिधि (मेनू, मूल्य निर्धारण, मीडिया, सेवा मानदंड) को अनुकूलित करते हुए।

segments.src: Tipping expectations, acceptable wait times, and how directly staff greet you all vary by country, and those are service attributes, not packaging.
segments.tr: टिपिंग की अपेक्षाएं, स्वीकार्य प्रतीक्षा समय, और कर्मचारी आपका अभिवादन कैसे करते हैं, ये सब देश के अनुसार अलग-अलग होते हैं, और ये सेवा विशेषताएं हैं, पैकेजिंग नहीं।

segments.src: **Decision 2: How do you enter?** Entry modes trade control against risk and commitment, roughly in this order:
segments.tr: **निर्णय 2: आप कैसे प्रवेश करते हैं?** प्रवेश मोड नियंत्रण को जोखिम और प्रतिबद्धता के विरुद्ध व्यापार करते हैं, मोटे तौर पर इस क्रम में:

segments.src: Exporting            low control, low risk, low commitment
segments.tr: Exporting            low control, low risk, low commitment

segments.src: Licensing            partner uses your IP for a fee
segments.tr: Licensing            partner uses your IP for a fee

segments.src: Franchising          partner runs your format under your rules
segments.tr: Franchising          partner runs your format under your rules

segments.src: Joint venture        shared ownership with a local firm
segments.tr: Joint venture        shared ownership with a local firm

segments.src: Wholly owned sub.    full control, full risk (also called FDI)
segments.tr: Wholly owned sub.    full control, full risk (also called FDI)

segments.src: Services complicate this.
segments.tr: सेवाएं इसे जटिल बनाती हैं।

segments.src: You can ship a container of sneakers; you can't ship a hotel stay.
segments.tr: आप स्नीकर्स का एक कंटेनर भेज सकते हैं; आप होटल में रहना नहीं भेज सकते।

segments.src: That's why service firms lean heavily on franchising, licensing, and joint ventures — they need people on the ground, and local partners bring real estate, regulatory knowledge, and labor practices you don't have.
segments.tr: इसीलिए सेवा कंपनियां फ्रैंचाइजिंग, लाइसेंसिंग और संयुक्त उद्यमों पर बहुत अधिक निर्भर करती हैं — उन्हें जमीन पर लोगों की जरूरत है, और स्थानीय भागीदार अचल संपत्ति, नियामक ज्ञान और श्रम प्रथाएं लाते हैं जो आपके पास नहीं हैं।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: Think about a Starbucks run in your own neighborhood, then think about Starbucks in Italy.
segments.tr: अपने पड़ोस में एक Starbucks दौड़ के बारे में सोचें, फिर इटली में Starbucks के बारे में सोचें।

segments.src: Locally, the 7Ps are all visible.
segments.tr: स्थानीय रूप से, 7Ps सभी दृश्यमान हैं।

segments.src: The **product** is a $6 latte, but also a chair and Wi-Fi.
segments.tr: **उत्पाद** एक $6 लैटे है, लेकिन एक कुर्सी और Wi-Fi भी है।

segments.src: **People**: the barista who writes your name on the cup.
segments.tr: **लोग**: बारिस्ता जो कप पर आपका नाम लिखता है।

segments.src: **Process**: mobile order-ahead, so the line isn't the experience.
segments.tr: **प्रक्रिया**: मोबाइल पूर्वानुमान, इसलिए लाइन अनुभव नहीं है।

segments.src: **Physical evidence**: the cup, the wood, the smell — tangible proof of an intangible thing.
segments.tr: **भौतिक साक्ष्य**: कप, लकड़ी, गंध — एक अमूर्त चीज का मूर्त प्रमाण।

segments.src: And **perishability** is why afternoon promotions exist at all; a 2:00 p.m.
segments.tr: और **नाशवानता** वह कारण है कि दोपहर की प्रचार बिल्कुल क्यों मौजूद हैं; एक 2:00 p.m.

segments.src: empty store is unrecoverable revenue, so you discount to shift demand into the trough rather than build more capacity for the 8:00 a.m.
segments.tr: खाली स्टोर अपूरणीय राजस्व है, इसलिए आप मांग को ट्राफ में स्थानांतरित करने के लिए छूट देते हैं बजाय 8:00 a.m. के लिए अधिक क्षमता बनाने के।

segments.src: peak.
segments.tr: शिखर के।

segments.src: Now go global.
segments.tr: अब वैश्विक जाएं।

segments.src: Starbucks entered Italy — a country with its own centuries-old espresso bar culture — only in September 2018, opening a Reserve Roastery in Milan rather than a standard store.
segments.tr: Starbucks इटली में प्रवेश किया — एक देश जिसकी अपनी सदियों पुरानी एस्प्रेसो बार संस्कृति है — केवल सितंबर 2018 में, मिलान में एक रिजर्व रोस्टरी खोलते हुए एक मानक स्टोर के बजाय।

segments.src: That's glocalization: keep the brand and quality standards, change the format and the pitch.
segments.tr: यह ग्लोकलाइजेशन है: ब्रांड और गुणवत्ता मानदंड रखें, प्रारूप और पिच बदलें।

segments.src: Elsewhere, Starbucks has used a mix of entry modes rather than one: company-owned stores in some markets, licensed stores operated by local partners in others, and a 50/50 joint venture with the Tata group in India (formed in 2012), where a local partner brought real estate and sourcing that a foreign entrant couldn't assemble quickly.
segments.tr: अन्यत्र, Starbucks ने एक के बजाय प्रवेश मोड के मिश्रण का उपयोग किया है: कुछ बाजारों में कंपनी के स्वामित्व वाले स्टोर, अन्य में स्थानीय भागीदारों द्वारा संचालित लाइसेंस प्राप्त स्टोर, और भारत में Tata समूह के साथ एक 50/50 संयुक्त उद्यम (2012 में गठित), जहां एक स्थानीय भागीदार ने अचल संपत्ति और सोर्सिंग लाई जो एक विदेशी प्रवेशकर्ता तेजी से एकत्र नहीं कर सकता था।

segments.src: The lesson isn't "copy Starbucks."
segments.tr: पाठ "Starbucks की कॉपी करना" नहीं है।

segments.src: It's that the same two questions — *what do we standardize?* and *how much control do we need on the ground?* — are the whole game, whether you're a coffee chain, a dental practice opening a second location in another state, or a SaaS company hiring its first support team in Berlin.
segments.tr: यह है कि वही दो सवाल — *हम क्या मानकीकृत करते हैं?* और *हमें जमीन पर कितना नियंत्रण चाहिए?* — पूरा खेल है, चाहे आप एक कॉफी चेन हों, एक दंत अभ्यास जो दूसरे राज्य में दूसरा स्थान खोल रहा है, या एक SaaS कंपनी जो बर्लिन में अपनी पहली सहायता टीम को नियुक्त कर रही है।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति सारांश

segments.src: 1. Services are intangible, variable, inseparable from delivery, and perishable — so quality is judged as *perceived performance minus expectation*, across five dimensions (RATER).
segments.tr: 1. सेवाएं अमूर्त, परिवर्तनशील, वितरण से अविभाज्य और नाशवान हैं — इसलिए गुणवत्ता को *माना गया प्रदर्शन घटा अपेक्षा* के रूप में न्याय किया जाता है, पांच आयामों में (RATER)।

segments.src: 2. The 4Ps stretch to 7Ps for services: add people, process, and physical evidence — because employees and choreography *are* the product.
segments.tr: 2. 4Ps सेवाओं के लिए 7Ps तक फैलते हैं: लोग, प्रक्रिया और भौतिक साक्ष्य जोड़ें — क्योंकि कर्मचारी और कोरियोग्राफी *उत्पाद हैं*।

segments.src: 3. Going global means choosing how much to standardize versus adapt, and choosing an entry mode along the control-versus-risk ladder; service firms lean toward franchising, licensing, and joint ventures because delivery can't be exported.
segments.tr: 3. वैश्विक जाना मतलब है कि कितना मानकीकृत करना बनाम अनुकूल करना चुनना, और नियंत्रण-बनाम-जोखिम सीढ़ी के साथ एक प्रवेश मोड चुनना; सेवा कंपनियां फ्रैंचाइजिंग, लाइसेंसिंग और संयुक्त उद्यमों की ओर झुकती हैं क्योंकि वितरण निर्यात नहीं किया जा सकता।

segments.tr: सेवाओं की कौन सी विशेषता यह है?

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **SERVQUAL** — A framework measuring service quality as the gap between customer expectations and perceptions, across five dimensions (reliability, assurance, tangibles, empathy, responsiveness).
segments.tr: - **SERVQUAL** — ग्राहक की अपेक्षाओं और धारणाओं के बीच के अंतर के रूप में सेवा गुणवत्ता को मापने के लिए एक ढांचा, पांच आयामों में (विश्वसनीयता, आश्वासन, मूर्त, सहानुभूति, प्रतिक्रिया)।

segments.src: - **Perishability** — The property that unused service capacity cannot be inventoried; unsold capacity is lost permanently.
segments.tr: - **नाशवानता** — वह संपत्ति कि अप्रयुक्त सेवा क्षमता को इन्वेंटरी नहीं किया जा सकता; बिना बिकी क्षमता स्थायी रूप से खो जाती है।

segments.src: - **Extended 7Ps** — The services marketing mix: the 4Ps plus people, process, and physical evidence.

es.title: [Marketing 101 #14] No Puedes Devolver un Corte de Cabello Malo: Marketing de Servicios e Internacionalización

segments.src: > When the product is a performance rather than a thing, quality becomes an experience you manage — and when you carry that experience across a border, you have to decide what stays the same and what bends.
segments.tr: > Cuando el producto es una actuación más que una cosa, la calidad se convierte en una experiencia que gestionas — y cuando llevas esa experiencia a través de una frontera, tienes que decidir qué permanece igual y qué se adapta.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: Most of what Americans spend money on isn't a thing you can put in a box.
segments.tr: La mayoría de lo que los estadounidenses gastan dinero no es algo que puedas poner en una caja.

segments.src: Haircuts, flights, checking accounts, dental cleanings, software subscriptions, a table at a restaurant — services make up the large majority of U.S.
segments.tr: Cortes de cabello, vuelos, cuentas corrientes, limpiezas dentales, suscripciones de software, una mesa en un restaurante — los servicios constituyen la gran mayoría de la

segments.src: economic activity and employment.
segments.tr: actividad económica y empleo.

segments.src: Marketing them works differently, for four stubborn reasons:
segments.tr: Comercializarlos funciona de manera diferente, por cuatro razones obstinadas:

segments.src: - **Intangibility.** You can't inspect a service before you buy it. You can hold a pair of shoes; you can't hold a root canal.
segments.tr: - **Intangibilidad.** No puedes inspeccionar un servicio antes de comprarlo. Puedes sostener un par de zapatos; no puedes sostener un tratamiento de conducto.

segments.src: - **Heterogeneity (variability).** The same barista, same store, different Tuesday — different experience. Humans deliver services, so quality wobbles.
segments.tr: - **Heterogeneidad (variabilidad).** El mismo barista, la misma tienda, un martes diferente — experiencia diferente. Los humanos entregan servicios, por lo que la calidad fluctúa.

segments.src: - **Inseparability.** Production and consumption happen at the same time. The customer is *inside the factory*, and so are the other customers.
segments.tr: - **Inseparabilidad.** La producción y el consumo ocurren al mismo tiempo. El cliente está *dentro de la fábrica*, al igual que los otros clientes.

segments.src: - **Perishability.** An empty seat on a 6:00 a.m. flight to Chicago can't be put in a warehouse and sold tomorrow. Unsold capacity is gone forever.
segments.tr: - **Perecedibilidad.** Un asiento vacío en un vuelo a las 6:00 a.m. a Chicago no puede ponerse en un almacén y venderse mañana. La capacidad no vendida desaparece para siempre.

segments.src: Because of this, service firms don't manage "quality" the way a factory does.
segments.tr: Por esto, las empresas de servicios no gestionan la "calidad" de la manera que lo hace una fábrica.

segments.src: The dominant framework, **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman, Zeithaml, and Berry, 1988), says customers judge service on five dimensions — often remembered as **RATER**:
segments.tr: El marco dominante, **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman, Zeithaml, y Berry, 1988), dice que los clientes juzgan el servicio en cinco dimensiones — a menudo recordadas como **RATER**:

segments.src: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?
segments.tr: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?

segments.src: Assurance       - do staff seem competent and trustworthy?
segments.tr: Assurance       - do staff seem competent and trustworthy?

segments.src: Tangibles       - how do the space, equipment, and people look?
segments.tr: Tangibles       - how do the space, equipment, and people look?

segments.src: Empathy         - was I treated as an individual?
segments.tr: Empathy         - was I treated as an individual?

segments.src: Responsiveness  - were they willing to help, promptly?
segments.tr: Responsiveness  - were they willing to help, promptly?

segments.src: The core idea is a gap: `Service quality = perceived performance - expectation`.
segments.tr: La idea central es una brecha: `Calidad del servicio = desempeño percibido - expectativa`.

segments.src: That's not a formula to compute so much as a warning.
segments.tr: Eso no es una fórmula para calcular sino una advertencia.

segments.src: You can improve a service and still lose customers, if your advertising raised expectations faster than your operation improved.
segments.tr: Puedes mejorar un servicio y aún perder clientes, si tu publicidad elevó las expectativas más rápido que tu operación mejoró.

segments.src: Under-promise is not a slogan; it's quality management.
segments.tr: Prometer menos no es un eslogan; es gestión de calidad.

segments.src: Because a service is a performance, the classic **4P** marketing mix (product, price, place, promotion) leaves out too much.
segments.tr: Porque un servicio es una actuación, la clásica mezcla de marketing de **4P** (producto, precio, lugar, promoción) deja fuera demasiado.

segments.src: Booms and Bitner (1981) added three, giving the **extended 7Ps**:
segments.tr: Booms y Bitner (1981) añadieron tres, dando las **7Ps extendidas**:

segments.src: - **People** — employees *are* the product. Front-line hiring and training is marketing spend, whether you book it that way or not.
segments.tr: - **Personas** — los empleados *son* el producto. La contratación y capacitación de primera línea es gasto de marketing, ya sea que lo registres de esa manera o no.

segments.src: - **Process** — the choreography of delivery: the online booking flow, the queue design, the way a refund is handled.
segments.tr: - **Proceso** — la coreografía de la entrega: el flujo de reserva en línea, el diseño de la cola, la manera en que se maneja un reembolso.

segments.src: - **Physical evidence** — the tangible cues that stand in for a product you can't see: the clean lobby, the branded cup, the confirmation email, the itemized receipt.
segments.tr: - **Evidencia Física** — las pistas tangibles que reemplazan a un producto que no puedes ver: el vestíbulo limpio, la taza de marca, el correo de confirmación, el recibo desglosado.

segments.src: **Global marketing** asks the same question one level up.
segments.tr: El **marketing global** hace la misma pregunta un nivel arriba.

segments.src: When you take an offering abroad, you face two decisions.
segments.tr: Cuando llevas una oferta al extranjero, enfrentas dos decisiones.

segments.src: **Decision 1: How much do you change?** Full **standardization** buys scale, a consistent brand, and lower cost.
segments.tr: **Decisión 1: ¿Cuánto cambias?** La **estandarización** completa compra escala, una marca consistente y menor costo.

segments.src: Full **adaptation** buys local fit.
segments.tr: La **adaptación** completa compra ajuste local.

segments.src: Almost everyone lands in between — **"glocalization"** — standardizing the core (brand, quality standards, core process) while adapting the periphery (menu, pricing, media, service norms).
segments.tr: Casi todos caen en el medio — **"glocalización"** — estandarizando el núcleo (marca, estándares de calidad, proceso central) mientras se adapta la periferia (menú, precios, medios, normas de servicio).

segments.src: Tipping expectations, acceptable wait times, and how directly staff greet you all vary by country, and those are service attributes, not packaging.
segments.tr: Las expectativas de propinas, los tiempos de espera aceptables y la forma en que el personal te saluda varían según el país, y esos son atributos de servicio, no de empaque.

segments.src: **Decision 2: How do you enter?** Entry modes trade control against risk and commitment, roughly in this order:
segments.tr: **Decisión 2: ¿Cómo entras?** Los modos de entrada intercambian control por riesgo y compromiso, más o menos en este orden:

segments.src: Exporting            low control, low risk, low commitment
segments.tr: Exporting            low control, low risk, low commitment

segments.src: Licensing            partner uses your IP for a fee
segments.tr: Licensing            partner uses your IP for a fee

segments.src: Franchising          partner runs your format under your rules
segments.tr: Franchising          partner runs your format under your rules

segments.src: Joint venture        shared ownership with a local firm
segments.tr: Joint venture        shared ownership with a local firm

segments.src: Wholly owned sub.    full control, full risk (also called FDI)
segments.tr: Wholly owned sub.    full control, full risk (also called FDI)

segments.src: Services complicate this.
segments.tr: Los servicios complican esto.

segments.src: You can ship a container of sneakers; you can't ship a hotel stay.
segments.tr: Puedes enviar un contenedor de zapatillas; no puedes enviar una estancia hotelera.

segments.src: That's why service firms lean heavily on franchising, licensing, and joint ventures — they need people on the ground, and local partners bring real estate, regulatory knowledge, and labor practices you don't have.
segments.tr: Por eso las empresas de servicios dependen mucho del franchising, licencias y asociaciones conjuntas — necesitan personas sobre el terreno, y los socios locales aportan bienes raíces, conocimiento regulatorio y prácticas laborales que no tienes.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Think about a Starbucks run in your own neighborhood, then think about Starbucks in Italy.
segments.tr: Piensa en una carrera a Starbucks en tu propio vecindario, luego piensa en Starbucks en Italia.

segments.src: Locally, the 7Ps are all visible.
segments.tr: Localmente, los 7Ps son todos visibles.

segments.src: The **product** is a $6 latte, but also a chair and Wi-Fi.
segments.tr: El **producto** es un latte de $6, pero también una silla y Wi-Fi.

segments.src: **People**: the barista who writes your name on the cup.
segments.tr: **Personas**: el barista que escribe tu nombre en la taza.

segments.src: **Process**: mobile order-ahead, so the line isn't the experience.
segments.tr: **Proceso**: pedido móvil por adelantado, así que la línea no es la experiencia.

segments.src: **Physical evidence**: the cup, the wood, the smell — tangible proof of an intangible thing.
segments.tr: **Evidencia Física**: la taza, la madera, el olor — prueba tangible de algo intangible.

segments.src: And **perishability** is why afternoon promotions exist at all; a 2:00 p.m.
segments.tr: Y la **perecedibilidad** es por qué existen promociones por la tarde; una tienda vacía a las 2:00 p.m.

segments.src: empty store is unrecoverable revenue, so you discount to shift demand into the trough rather than build more capacity for the 8:00 a.m.
segments.tr: es ingresos irrecuperables, así que haces un descuento para desplazar la demanda al valle en lugar de construir más capacidad para el

segments.src: peak.
segments.tr: pico.

segments.src: Now go global.
segments.tr: Ahora ve al mundo.

segments.src: Starbucks entered Italy — a country with its own centuries-old espresso bar culture — only in September 2018, opening a Reserve Roastery in Milan rather than a standard store.
segments.tr: Starbucks entró en Italia — un país con su propia cultura de bares de espresso centenarios — solo en septiembre de 2018, abriendo una Reserve Roastery en Milán en lugar de una tienda estándar.

segments.src: That's glocalization: keep the brand and quality standards, change the format and the pitch.
segments.tr: Eso es glocalización: mantén la marca y los estándares de calidad, cambia el formato y la propuesta.

segments.src: Elsewhere, Starbucks has used a mix of entry modes rather than one: company-owned stores in some markets, licensed stores operated by local partners in others, and a 50/50 joint venture with the Tata group in India (formed in 2012), where a local partner brought real estate and sourcing that a foreign entrant couldn't assemble quickly.
segments.tr: En otros lugares, Starbucks ha utilizado una mezcla de modos de entrada en lugar de uno: tiendas de propiedad de la empresa en algunos mercados, tiendas con licencia operadas por socios locales en otros, y una asociación conjunta al 50/50 con el grupo Tata en India (formada en 2012), donde un socio local aportó bienes raíces y abastecimiento que un participante extranjero no podría reunir rápidamente.

segments.src: The lesson isn't "copy Starbucks."
segments.tr: La lección no es "copiar Starbucks".

segments.src: It's that the same two questions — *what do we standardize?* and *how much control do we need on the ground?* — are the whole game, whether you're a coffee chain, a dental practice opening a second location in another state, or a SaaS company hiring its first support team in Berlin.
segments.tr: Es que las mismas dos preguntas — *¿qué estandarizamos?* y *¿cuánto control necesitamos sobre el terreno?* — son todo el juego, ya sea que seas una cadena de café, una práctica dental abriendo una segunda ubicación en otro estado, o una empresa SaaS contratando su primer equipo de soporte en Berlín.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen de Tres Líneas

segments.src: 1. Services are intangible, variable, inseparable from delivery, and perishable — so quality is judged as *perceived performance minus expectation*, across five dimensions (RATER).
segments.tr: 1. Los servicios son intangibles, variables, inseparables de la entrega y perecederos — por lo que la calidad se juzga como *desempeño percibido menos expectativa*, en cinco dimensiones (RATER).

segments.src: 2. The 4Ps stretch to 7Ps for services: add people, process, and physical evidence — because employees and choreography *are* the product.
segments.tr: 2. Los 4Ps se estiran a 7Ps para servicios: añade personas, proceso y evidencia física — porque los empleados y la coreografía *son* el producto.

segments.src: 3. Going global means choosing how much to standardize versus adapt, and choosing an entry mode along the control-versus-risk ladder; service firms lean toward franchising, licensing, and joint ventures because delivery can't be exported.
segments.tr: 3. Ir al mundo significa elegir cuánto estandarizar versus adaptar, y elegir un modo de entrada a lo largo de la escalera de control-versus-riesgo; las empresas de servicios se inclinan hacia el franchising, licencias y asociaciones conjuntas porque la entrega no se puede exportar.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de Hoy

segments.src: - **SERVQUAL** — A framework measuring service quality as the gap between customer expectations and perceptions, across five dimensions (reliability, assurance, tangibles, empathy, responsiveness).
segments.tr: - **SERVQUAL** — Un marco que mide la calidad del servicio como la brecha entre las expectativas y percepciones del cliente, en cinco dimensiones (confiabilidad, seguridad, elementos tangibles, empatía, capacidad de respuesta).

segments.src: - **Perishability** — The property that unused service capacity cannot be inventoried; unsold capacity is lost permanently.
segments.tr: - **Perecedibilidad** — La propiedad de que la capacidad de servicio no utilizada no puede ser inventariada; la capacidad no vendida se pierde permanentemente.

segments.src: - **Extended 7Ps** — The services marketing mix: the 4Ps plus people, process, and physical evidence.
segments.tr: - **7Ps Extendidas** — La mezcla de marketing de servicios: los 4Ps más personas, proceso y evidencia física.

segments.src: - **Physical evidence** — Tangible cues (facilities, uniforms, receipts, packaging) that customers use to infer the quality of an intangible service.
segments.tr: - **Evidencia Física** — Pistas tangibles (instalaciones, uniformes, recibos, empaque) que los clientes utilizan para inferir la calidad de un servicio intangible.

segments.src: - **Glocalization** — Standardizing a global brand's core while adapting local elements such as menu, pricing, and communication.
segments.tr: - **Glocalización** — Estandarizar el núcleo de una marca global mientras se adaptan elementos locales como menú, precios y comunicación.

segments.src: - **Entry mode** — The structural choice for entering a foreign market (exporting, licensing, franchising, joint venture, wholly owned subsidiary), trading control against risk and commitment.
segments.tr: - **Modo de entrada** — La elección estructural para entrar a un mercado extranjero (exportación, licencias, franchising, asociación conjunta, subsidiaria de propiedad total), intercambiando control por riesgo y compromiso.

segments.src: Services are consumed as they're produced, so idle capacity can't be stored; this is why airlines, hotels, and salons manage demand with time-based pricing.
segments.tr: Los servicios se consumen según se producen, por lo que la capacidad ociosa no puede almacenarse; por eso las aerolíneas, hoteles y salones gestionan la demanda con precios basados en el tiempo.

segments.src: 2 — (a) People, Process, Physical evidence, added by Booms and Bitner (1981) precisely because service delivery depends on staff, choreography, and tangible cues.
segments.tr: 2 — (a) Personas, Proceso, Evidencia Física, añadidos por Booms y Bitner (1981) precisamente porque la entrega de servicios depende del personal, la coreografía y las pistas tangibles.

segments.src: Entry modes form a ladder: exporting is low control and low risk; a joint venture shares ownership and gives more operational control, but commits capital and exposes you to partner and market risk; a wholly owned subsidiary sits at the far end of both.*
segments.tr: Los modos de entrada forman una escalera: la exportación es bajo control y bajo riesgo; una asociación conjunta comparte la propiedad y da más control operativo, pero compromete capital y te expone al riesgo del socio y del mercado; una subsidiaria de propiedad total se encuentra en el extremo más alejado de ambas.*

segments.tr: يعمل تسويقها بشكل مختلف، لأربعة أسباب عنيدة:

segments.src: - **Intangibility.** You can't inspect a service before you buy it. You can hold a pair of shoes; you can't hold a root canal.
segments.tr: - **عدم الملموسية.** لا يمكنك فحص خدمة قبل شرائها. يمكنك الإمساك بزوج من الأحذية؛ لا يمكنك الإمساك بمعالجة جذر السن.

segments.src: - **Heterogeneity (variability).** The same barista, same store, different Tuesday — different experience. Humans deliver services, so quality wobbles.
segments.tr: - **عدم التجانس (التباين).** نفس بارستا، نفس المتجر، يوم ثلاثاء مختلف — تجربة مختلفة. البشر يقدمون الخدمات، لذا تتقلب الجودة.

segments.src: - **Inseparability.** Production and consumption happen at the same time. The customer is *inside the factory*, and so are the other customers.
segments.tr: - **عدم الانفصال.** الإنتاج والاستهلاك يحدثان في الوقت ذاته. العميل *داخل المصنع*، وكذلك العملاء الآخرون.

segments.src: - **Perishability.** An empty seat on a 6:00 a.m. flight to Chicago can't be put in a warehouse and sold tomorrow. Unsold capacity is gone forever.
segments.tr: - **قابلية التلف.** لا يمكن وضع مقعد فارغ في رحلة الساعة 6:00 صباحًا إلى شيكاغو في مستودع وبيعه غدًا. السعة غير المباعة تختفي إلى الأبد.

segments.src: Because of this, service firms don't manage "quality" the way a factory does.
segments.tr: لهذا السبب، لا تدير شركات الخدمات "الجودة" بالطريقة التي يفعلها المصنع.

segments.src: The dominant framework, **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman, Zeithaml, and Berry, 1988), says customers judge service on five dimensions — often remembered as **RATER**:
segments.tr: الإطار السائد، **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman و Zeithaml و Berry، 1988)، يقول إن العملاء يحكمون على الخدمة في خمسة أبعاد — غالبًا ما يتذكرونها باسم **RATER**:

segments.src: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?
segments.tr: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?

segments.src: Assurance       - do staff seem competent and trustworthy?
segments.tr: Assurance       - do staff seem competent and trustworthy?

segments.src: Tangibles       - how do the space, equipment, and people look?
segments.tr: Tangibles       - how do the space, equipment, and people look?

segments.src: Empathy         - was I treated as an individual?
segments.tr: Empathy         - was I treated as an individual?

segments.src: Responsiveness  - were they willing to help, promptly?
segments.tr: Responsiveness  - were they willing to help, promptly?

segments.src: The core idea is a gap: `Service quality = perceived performance - expectation`.
segments.tr: الفكرة الأساسية هي فجوة: `جودة الخدمة = الأداء المتصور - التوقعات`.

segments.src: That's not a formula to compute so much as a warning.
segments.tr: هذا ليس صيغة لحسابها بقدر ما هو تحذير.

segments.src: You can improve a service and still lose customers, if your advertising raised expectations faster than your operation improved.
segments.tr: يمكنك تحسين خدمة وفقدان العملاء في الوقت ذاته، إذا رفع إعلانك التوقعات أسرع مما حسّنت عملياتك.

segments.src: Under-promise is not a slogan; it's quality management.
segments.tr: الوعود المنخفضة ليست شعارًا؛ إنها إدارة الجودة.

segments.src: Because a service is a performance, the classic **4P** marketing mix (product, price, place, promotion) leaves out too much.
segments.tr: لأن الخدمة هي أداء، مزيج **4P** التسويقي الكلاسيكي (المنتج والسعر والمكان والترويج) يترك الكثير جانبًا.

segments.src: Booms and Bitner (1981) added three, giving the **extended 7Ps**:
segments.tr: أضاف Booms و Bitner (1981) ثلاثة، مما أعطى **7Ps الموسع**:

segments.src: - **People** — employees *are* the product. Front-line hiring and training is marketing spend, whether you book it that way or not.
segments.tr: - **الأشخاص** — الموظفون *هم* المنتج. استقطاب واستدراج موظفي الواجهة الأمامية وتدريبهم هي نفقات تسويق، سواء حسبتها بهذه الطريقة أم لا.

segments.src: - **Process** — the choreography of delivery: the online booking flow, the queue design, the way a refund is handled.
segments.tr: - **العملية** — حركات الأداء: تدفق الحجز عبر الإنترنت وتصميم الطابور وطريقة التعامل مع المبالغ المستردة.

segments.src: - **Physical evidence** — the tangible cues that stand in for a product you can't see: the clean lobby, the branded cup, the confirmation email, the itemized receipt.
segments.tr: - **الأدلة المادية** — الإشارات الملموسة التي تقف بدلاً من منتج لا يمكنك رؤيته: الردهة النظيفة والكوب الموسوم والبريد الإلكتروني للتأكيد والإيصال المفصل.

segments.src: **Global marketing** asks the same question one level up.
segments.tr: **التسويق العالمي** يطرح نفس السؤال مستوى واحد أعلى.

segments.src: When you take an offering abroad, you face two decisions.
segments.tr: عندما تأخذ عرضًا إلى الخارج، تواجه قرارين.

segments.src: **Decision 1: How much do you change?** Full **standardization** buys scale, a consistent brand, and lower cost.
segments.tr: **القرار 1: إلى أي مدى تتغير؟** التوحيد **الكامل** يشتري الحجم والعلامة التجارية المتسقة والتكلفة المنخفضة.

segments.src: Full **adaptation** buys local fit.
segments.tr: **التكيف الكامل** يشتري المطابقة المحلية.

segments.src: Almost everyone lands in between — **"glocalization"** — standardizing the core (brand, quality standards, core process) while adapting the periphery (menu, pricing, media, service norms).
segments.tr: يهبط الجميع تقريبًا في المنتصف — **"glocalization"** — توحيد الجوهر (العلامة التجارية ومعايير الجودة والعملية الأساسية) مع تكييف الأطراف (القائمة والسعر والإعلام ومعايير الخدمة).

segments.src: Tipping expectations, acceptable wait times, and how directly staff greet you all vary by country, and those are service attributes, not packaging.
segments.tr: البقشيش والتوقعات وأوقات الانتظار المقبولة وطريقة تحية الموظفين لك تختلف حسب البلد، وهذه كلها سمات خدمة وليست تغليفًا.

segments.src: **Decision 2: How do you enter?** Entry modes trade control against risk and commitment, roughly in this order:
segments.tr: **القرار 2: كيف تدخل؟** طرق الدخول تتاجر بالسيطرة مقابل المخاطر والالتزام، تقريبًا بهذا الترتيب:

segments.src: Exporting            low control, low risk, low commitment
segments.tr: Exporting            low control, low risk, low commitment

segments.src: Licensing            partner uses your IP for a fee
segments.tr: Licensing            partner uses your IP for a fee

segments.src: Franchising          partner runs your format under your rules
segments.tr: Franchising          partner runs your format under your rules

segments.src: Joint venture        shared ownership with a local firm
segments.tr: Joint venture        shared ownership with a local firm

segments.src: Wholly owned sub.    full control, full risk (also called FDI)
segments.tr: Wholly owned sub.    full control, full risk (also called FDI)

segments.src: Services complicate this.
segments.tr: الخدمات تعقد هذا.

segments.src: You can ship a container of sneakers; you can't ship a hotel stay.
segments.tr: يمكنك شحن حاوية من الأحذية الرياضية؛ لا يمكنك شحن إقامة فندقية.

segments.src: That's why service firms lean heavily on franchising, licensing, and joint ventures — they need people on the ground, and local partners bring real estate, regulatory knowledge, and labor practices you don't have.
segments.tr: لهذا تعتمد شركات الخدمات بشدة على الامتيازات والترخيص والمشاريع المشتركة — فهي بحاجة إلى أشخاص على الأرض، والشركاء المحليون يجلبون العقارات والمعرفة التنظيمية وممارسات العمل التي لا تملكها.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Think about a Starbucks run in your own neighborhood, then think about Starbucks in Italy.
segments.tr: فكر في رحلة Starbucks في حيك الخاص، ثم فكر في Starbucks في إيطاليا.

segments.src: Locally, the 7Ps are all visible.
segments.tr: محليًا، تكون 7Ps مرئية جميعًا.

segments.src: The **product** is a $6 latte, but also a chair and Wi-Fi.
segments.tr: **المنتج** هو لاتيه بقيمة 6 دولارات، لكنه أيضًا كرسي و Wi-Fi.

segments.src: **People**: the barista who writes your name on the cup.
segments.tr: **الأشخاص**: بارستا الذي يكتب اسمك على الكوب.

segments.src: **Process**: mobile order-ahead, so the line isn't the experience.
segments.tr: **العملية**: الطلب المسبق عبر الهاتف المحمول، بحيث لا تكون الخط التجربة.

segments.src: **Physical evidence**: the cup, the wood, the smell — tangible proof of an intangible thing.
segments.tr: **الأدلة المادية**: الكوب والخشب والرائحة — إثبات ملموس لشيء غير ملموس.

segments.src: And **perishability** is why afternoon promotions exist at all; a 2:00 p.m.
segments.tr: و **قابلية التلف** هي السبب في وجود عروض ما بعد الظهر؛ متجر في الساعة 2:00 مساءً

segments.src: empty store is unrecoverable revenue, so you discount to shift demand into the trough rather than build more capacity for the 8:00 a.m.
segments.tr: فارغ هو إيراد لا يمكن استرجاعه، لذا تقدم خصمًا لتحويل الطلب إلى القاع بدلاً من بناء مزيد من السعة للساعة 8:00 صباحًا

segments.src: peak.
segments.tr: الذروة.

segments.src: Now go global.
segments.tr: الآن اذهب عالميًا.

segments.src: Starbucks entered Italy — a country with its own centuries-old espresso bar culture — only in September 2018, opening a Reserve Roastery in Milan rather than a standard store.
segments.tr: دخلت Starbucks إيطاليا — دولة لها ثقافة حانة إسبريسو عمرها قرون — فقط في سبتمبر 2018، وفتحت محمصة محفوظة في ميلان بدلاً من متجر عادي.

segments.src: That's glocalization: keep the brand and quality standards, change the format and the pitch.
segments.tr: هذا هو glocalization: احتفظ بالعلامة التجارية ومعايير الجودة، غيّر الصيغة والعرض.

segments.src: Elsewhere, Starbucks has used a mix of entry modes rather than one: company-owned stores in some markets, licensed stores operated by local partners in others, and a 50/50 joint venture with the Tata group in India (formed in 2012), where a local partner brought real estate and sourcing that a foreign entrant couldn't assemble quickly.
segments.tr: في أماكن أخرى، استخدمت Starbucks مزيجًا من أنماط الدخول بدلاً من واحد: متاجر مملوكة للشركة في بعض الأسواق، ومتاجر مرخصة يديرها شركاء محليون في أماكن أخرى، ومشروع مشترك 50/50 مع مجموعة Tata في الهند (تشكل في 2012)، حيث جلب الشريك المحلي العقارات والمصادر التي لم يستطع المدخل الأجنبي تجميعها بسرعة.

segments.src: The lesson isn't "copy Starbucks."
segments.tr: الدرس ليس "انسخ Starbucks."

segments.src: It's that the same two questions — *what do we standardize?* and *how much control do we need on the ground?* — are the whole game, whether you're a coffee chain, a dental practice opening a second location in another state, or a SaaS company hiring its first support team in Berlin.
segments.tr: الأمر أن نفس السؤالين — *ما الذي نوحده؟* و *كم السيطرة التي نحتاجها على الأرض؟* — هما اللعبة برمتها، سواء كنت سلسلة قهوة أو عيادة طب أسنان تفتح موقعًا ثانيًا في ولاية أخرى، أو شركة SaaS توظف فريق دعمها الأول في برلين.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص ثلاثي السطور

segments.src: 1. Services are intangible, variable, inseparable from delivery, and perishable — so quality is judged as *perceived performance minus expectation*, across five dimensions (RATER).
segments.tr: 1. الخدمات غير ملموسة ومتغيرة وغير قابلة للفصل عن التسليم وقابلة للتلف — لذا يتم الحكم على الجودة على أنها *الأداء المتصور ناقصًا التوقعات*، عبر خمسة أبعاد (RATER).

segments.src: 2. The 4Ps stretch to 7Ps for services: add people, process, and physical evidence — because employees and choreography *are* the product.
segments.tr: 2. تمتد 4Ps إلى 7Ps للخدمات: أضف الأشخاص والعملية والأدلة المادية — لأن الموظفين والحركات *هم* المنتج.

segments.src: 3. Going global means choosing how much to standardize versus adapt, and choosing an entry mode along the control-versus-risk ladder; service firms lean toward franchising, licensing, and joint ventures because delivery can't be exported.
segments.tr: 3. الذهاب عالميًا يعني اختيار مقدار التوحيد مقابل التكيف، واختيار طريقة دخول على سلم السيطرة مقابل المخاطر؛ تميل شركات الخدمات نحو الامتيازات والترخيص والمشاريع المشتركة لأن التسليم لا يمكن تصديره.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 شروط اليوم

segments.src: - **SERVQUAL** — A framework measuring service quality as the gap between customer expectations and perceptions, across five dimensions (reliability, assurance, tangibles, empathy, responsiveness).
segments.tr: - **SERVQUAL** — إطار قياس جودة الخدمة كالفجوة بين توقعات العملاء وتصوراتهم، عبر خمسة أبعاد (الموثوقية والضمان والملموسات والتعاطف والاستجابة).

segments.src: - **Perishability** — The property that unused service capacity cannot be inventoried; unsold capacity is lost permanently.
segments.tr: - **قابلية التلف** — الخاصية التي لا يمكن فيها حصر السعة غير المستخدمة للخدمة؛ السعة غير المباعة تُفقد بشكل دائم.

segments.src: - **Extended 7Ps** — The services marketing mix: the 4Ps plus people, process, and physical evidence.
segments.tr: - **7Ps الموسع** — مزيج تسويق الخدمات: 4Ps بالإضافة إلى الأشخاص والعملية والأدلة المادية.

segments.src: - **Physical evidence** — Tangible cues (facilities, uniforms, receipts, packaging) that customers use to infer the quality of an intangible service.
segments.tr: - **الأدلة المادية** — إشارات ملموسة (المنشآت والزي الرسمي والإيصالات والتغليف) التي يستخدمها العملاء للاستدلال على جودة الخدمة غير الملموسة.

segments.src: - **Glocalization** — Standardizing a global brand's core while adapting local elements such as menu, pricing, and communication.
segments.tr: - **Glocalization** — توحيد جوهر العلامة التجارية العالمية مع تكييف العناصر المحلية مثل القائمة والسعر والاتصالات.

segments.src: - **Entry mode** — The structural choice for entering a foreign market (exporting, licensing, franchising, joint venture, wholly owned subsidiary), trading control against risk and commitment.
segments.tr: - **طريقة الدخول** — الاختيار الهيكلي لدخول سوق أجنبي (الصادرات والترخيص والامتياز والمشروع المشترك والشركة التابعة المملوكة بالكامل)، يتاجر بالسيطرة مقابل المخاطر والالتزام.

segments.src: *Answers: 1 — (c) Perishability.
segments.tr: *الإجابات: 1 — (ج) قابلية التلف.

segments.src: Services are consumed as they're produced, so idle capacity can't be stored; this is why airlines, hotels, and salons manage demand with time-based pricing.
segments.tr: يتم استهلاك الخدمات عند إنتاجها، لذا لا يمكن تخزين السعة الخاملة؛ هذا هو السبب في أن شركات الطيران والفنادق والصالونات تدير الطلب من خلال التسعير القائم على الوقت.

segments.src: 2 — (a) People, Process, Physical evidence, added by Booms and Bitner (1981) precisely because service delivery depends on staff, choreography, and tangible cues.
segments.tr: 2 — (أ) الأشخاص والعملية والأدلة المادية، التي أضافها Booms و Bitner (1981) بالضبط لأن تسليم الخدمة يعتمد على الموظفين والحركات والإشارات الملموسة.

segments.src: Entry modes form a ladder: exporting is low control and low risk; a joint venture shares ownership and gives more operational control, but commits capital and exposes you to partner and market risk; a wholly owned subsidiary sits at the far end of both.*
segments.tr: تشكل طرق الدخول سلمًا: الصادرات هي سيطرة منخفضة ومخاطر منخفضة؛ المشروع المشترك يشارك الملكية ويعطي سيطرة عملياتية أكثر، لكنه يلتزم رأس المال ويعرضك لمخاطر الشريك والسوق؛ الشركة التابعة المملوكة بالكامل تقع في الطرف البعيد من الاثنين.*

fr.title: [Marketing 101 #14] On ne peut pas rendre une mauvaise coupe de cheveux : Le marketing des services et l'expansion mondiale

segments.src: > When the product is a performance rather than a thing, quality becomes an experience you manage — and when you carry that experience across a border, you have to decide what stays the same and what bends.
segments.tr: > Quand le produit est une prestation plutôt qu'une chose, la qualité devient une expérience que vous gérez — et quand vous transportez cette expérience au-delà d'une frontière, vous devez décider ce qui reste pareil et ce qui s'adapte.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: Most of what Americans spend money on isn't a thing you can put in a box.
segments.tr: La plupart de ce sur quoi les Américains dépensent de l'argent n'est pas une chose qu'on peut mettre dans une boîte.

segments.src: Haircuts, flights, checking accounts, dental cleanings, software subscriptions, a table at a restaurant — services make up the large majority of U.S.
segments.tr: Les coupes de cheveux, les vols, les comptes courants, les nettoyages dentaires, les abonnements logiciels, une table au restaurant — les services constituent la grande majorité de l'économie U.S.

segments.src: economic activity and employment.
segments.tr: et de l'emploi.

segments.src: Marketing them works differently, for four stubborn reasons:
segments.tr: Les commercialiser fonctionne différemment, pour quatre raisons tenaces :

segments.src: - **Intangibility.** You can't inspect a service before you buy it. You can hold a pair of shoes; you can't hold a root canal.
segments.tr: - **Intangibilité.** Vous ne pouvez pas inspecter un service avant de l'acheter. Vous pouvez tenir une paire de chaussures ; vous ne pouvez pas tenir un détartrage dentaire.

segments.src: - **Heterogeneity (variability).** The same barista, same store, different Tuesday — different experience. Humans deliver services, so quality wobbles.
segments.tr: - **Hétérogénéité (variabilité).** Le même barista, le même magasin, un mardi différent — une expérience différente. Les humains fournissent les services, donc la qualité varie.

segments.src: - **Inseparability.** Production and consumption happen at the same time. The customer is *inside the factory*, and so are the other customers.
segments.tr: - **Inséparabilité.** La production et la consommation se produisent au même moment. Le client est *à l'intérieur de l'usine*, tout comme les autres clients.

segments.src: - **Perishability.** An empty seat on a 6:00 a.m. flight to Chicago can't be put in a warehouse and sold tomorrow. Unsold capacity is gone forever.
segments.tr: - **Caractère périssable.** Une place vide dans un vol de 6h00 du matin pour Chicago ne peut pas être mise dans un entrepôt et vendue demain. La capacité invendue est partie pour toujours.

segments.src: Because of this, service firms don't manage "quality" the way a factory does.
segments.tr: Pour cette raison, les entreprises de services ne gèrent pas la « qualité » comme le ferait une usine.

segments.src: The dominant framework, **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman, Zeithaml, and Berry, 1988), says customers judge service on five dimensions — often remembered as **RATER**:
segments.tr: Le cadre dominant, **SERVQUAL** (Parasuraman, Zeithaml, et Berry, 1988), dit que les clients jugent le service sur cinq dimensions — souvent mémorisées comme **RATER** :

segments.src: Reliability     - did they do what they promised, accurately?
